title: Powell Expedition geologic time half-life
learningObjectives: Explain that a half-life is the time for half of the parent isotopes to decay to a stable daughter isotope.
Use the relation N = N0(1/2)^(t/T) to calculate the amount of parent isotope remaining after elapsed time t.
Interpret a parent-daughter ratio of one-eighth parent remaining as three half-lives, about 2.13 billion years for uranium-235.

explanations.text: A half-life is the characteristic time for half of the original parent isotopes to decay to a stable daughter isotope.

evidence.quote: A half-life is the length of time it takes for half of the number of original, or parent, isotopes to decay to a stable daughter isotope.

explanations.text: Uranium-235 decays to lead-207 with a characteristic half-life of 710 million years, providing a clock for dating rocks.

evidence.quote: For example, uranium-235 is an unstable parent isotope that decays to lead-207, with a half-life of 710 million years.

explanations.text: When only one-eighth of the parent remains, three half-lives have passed, which for uranium-235 is about 2.13 billion years.

evidence.quote: If seven-eighths of the total is Lead-207 and one-eighth is uranium-235, how old is the rock?
Answer: three half-lives old, or 2.13 billion years old.

predictions.prompt: A uranium-235 sample starts with 800 grams and has a half-life of 710 million years. After 2.13 billion years, how much parent uranium remains?
